title: DNA, Genes and Protein Synthesis
seo_title: Year 12 Biology: DNA, Genes and Protein Synthesis Worksheets (Australian Curriculum)
standard_code: Biology Unit 3: DNA, genes and the continuity of life
standard_text: The structure of DNA and its replication; genes, chromosomes and the genetic code; transcription and translation in protein synthesis; introns, exons and gene regulation; how gene expression leads to differentiation. (Senior Secondary Biology, Unit 3: Heredity and continuity of life)
meta_desc: Free Year 12 Biology worksheets on DNA and protein synthesis: base pairing, replication, the genetic code, transcription, translation, codons, anticodons and gene expression. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: A pairs with T (U in RNA); C pairs with G.
body_html:
How to think about it

DNA is a double helix of nucleotides; A pairs with T and C with G. Replication is semi-conservative. A gene is a DNA sequence that codes for a protein.

In transcription, RNA polymerase makes mRNA from the template strand (U replaces T); introns are removed. In translation, ribosomes read mRNA codons and tRNA anticodons bring the amino acids. Cells with the same DNA differ because they express different genes.

Example

Template strand TAC GGA TTC. mRNA?

complementary bases, U for A

Answer: AUG CCU AAG

Example

mRNA AUG CCU AAG: how many amino acids?

3 codons

Answer: 3 amino acids

Common mistakes

  • Writing T instead of U in mRNA.
  • Saying genes are made of protein.
  • Mixing up codons (mRNA) and anticodons (tRNA).

faq.q: Why is the genetic code called universal?
faq.a: Almost all organisms use the same codons for the same amino acids, which is why a human gene can be expressed in bacteria.

faq.q: Where do transcription and translation happen in eukaryotes?
faq.a: Transcription in the nucleus; translation on ribosomes in the cytoplasm or on the rough endoplasmic reticulum.

items.q: One DNA strand has the base sequence ACCACGGAGGTC. What is the sequence of the complementary strand?
items.e: A pairs with T and G pairs with C.

items.q: Which bases pair in DNA?
c: adenine with thymine, and cytosine with guanine
every base can pair with any other
adenine with uracil, and cytosine with guanine
adenine with cytosine, and guanine with thymine
items.e: A–T has two hydrogen bonds, C–G three.

items.q: In the DNA of a fish, 34% of the bases are adenine. What percentage are cytosine?
items.e: A + T = 68%, so G + C = 32%, and cytosine = half of that: 16.0%.

items.q: What happens during translation?
c: ribosomes read mRNA codons and tRNA brings the matching amino acids
items.e: Peptide bonds join the amino acids.

items.q: What are Okazaki fragments?
c: short DNA pieces made on the lagging strand
items.e: DNA ligase joins them.

items.q: One DNA strand has the base sequence GGTCCTCTCA. What is the sequence of the complementary strand?
items.e: A pairs with T and G pairs with C.

items.q: A DNA segment has 640 base pairs. How many hydrogen bonds hold it together if 30% of its bases are adenine?
items.e: A = T = 30%, G = C = 20%. A–T pairs = 384 (2 bonds), G–C pairs = 256 (3 bonds): total = 1536.

items.q: What does semi-conservative replication mean?
c: each new DNA molecule has one original strand and one new strand
both strands of the new molecule are new
items.e: Shown by the Meselson–Stahl experiment.

items.q: One DNA strand has the base sequence ATTCGTATGA. What is the sequence of the complementary strand?
items.e: A pairs with T and G pairs with C.

items.q: What are the three parts of a DNA nucleotide?
c: a phosphate group, deoxyribose sugar and a nitrogenous base
an amino acid, a sugar and a base
a fatty acid, glycerol and a phosphate
items.e: RNA nucleotides have ribose instead.

items.q: Why is the genetic code called degenerate?
c: each codon codes for several amino acids
most amino acids are coded for by more than one codon
items.e: There are 64 codons for 20 amino acids.

items.q: A DNA segment has 3150 base pairs. How many hydrogen bonds hold it together if 30% of its bases are adenine?
items.e: A = T = 30%, G = C = 20%. A–T pairs = 1890 (2 bonds), G–C pairs = 1260 (3 bonds): total = 7560.

items.q: Why is the genetic code called degenerate?
c: most amino acids are coded by more than one codon
items.e: There are 61 sense codons for 20 amino acids.

items.q: What is the function of tRNA?
c: it carries the code from DNA
it brings the correct amino acid to the ribosome by matching its anticodon to the codon
items.e: It has a clover-leaf shape.

items.q: What is the genetic code?
c: the order of chromosomes in a cell
the number of genes in an organism
the sequence of base triplets (codons) that specifies amino acids
items.e: It is universal and degenerate.

items.q: A section of double-stranded DNA is 150 base pairs long. How many nucleotides does it contain?
items.e: Each base pair is two nucleotides: 300.

items.q: One DNA strand has the base sequence AGGCTGTCC. What is the sequence of the complementary strand?
items.e: A pairs with T and G pairs with C.

items.q: What happens during transcription?
c: amino acids are joined at the ribosome
an mRNA copy of a gene is made from the DNA template strand in the nucleus
DNA is copied before cell division
items.e: RNA polymerase does this.

items.q: A section of double-stranded DNA is 240 base pairs long. How many nucleotides does it contain?
items.e: Each base pair is two nucleotides: 480.

items.q: What is the backbone of a DNA strand made of?
items.e: The bases point inwards.

items.q: A DNA strand reads AGA GGA TAA. What is the complementary DNA strand?
items.e: In DNA, A pairs with T and G pairs with C.

items.q: A gene is 450 bases long, of which 300 bases are in introns. How many amino acids does it code for? (Ignore start and stop codons.)
items.e: Only exons are translated: 150 bases ÷ 3 = 50.

items.q: A gene is 2400 bases long. How many amino acids does it code for? (Ignore start and stop codons.)
items.e: Only exons are translated: 2400 bases ÷ 3 = 800.

items.q: What are introns?
c: the coding sections that stay in mRNA
non-coding sections of a gene that are removed from pre-mRNA
items.e: The exons are joined in splicing.

items.q: What is a gene?
c: a section of DNA that codes for a protein or functional RNA
items.e: Humans have about 20 000 protein-coding genes.

items.q: A DNA strand reads CAT GTC. What is the complementary DNA strand?
items.e: In DNA, A pairs with T and G pairs with C.

items.q: What is the structure of a eukaryotic chromosome?
c: a long DNA molecule wound around histone proteins
a circular DNA molecule with no proteins
items.e: Prokaryotes have circular DNA and often plasmids.

items.q: How is DNA stored in eukaryotic cells?
c: as long linear molecules wound around histone proteins
as short circular molecules without proteins
items.e: Prokaryotes have circular DNA not linked to histones.

items.q: A DNA strand reads CGA ATA ATG. What is the complementary DNA strand?
items.e: In DNA, A pairs with T and G pairs with C.

items.q: What is a promoter?
c: a DNA sequence near the start of a gene where RNA polymerase binds
items.e: Transcription factors help RNA polymerase bind.

items.q: A gene is 1200 bases long, of which 600 bases are in introns. How many amino acids does it code for? (Ignore start and stop codons.)
items.e: Only exons are translated: 600 bases ÷ 3 = 200.

items.q: A gene is 1500 bases long. How many amino acids does it code for? (Ignore start and stop codons.)
items.e: Only exons are translated: 1500 bases ÷ 3 = 500.

items.q: What does RNA polymerase do?
c: joins RNA nucleotides complementary to the template strand
items.e: It moves along the gene.

items.q: A DNA strand reads GAT GCA GCT. What is the complementary DNA strand?
items.e: In DNA, A pairs with T and G pairs with C.

items.q: A gene is 600 bases long, of which 300 bases are in introns. How many amino acids does it code for? (Ignore start and stop codons.)
items.e: Only exons are translated: 300 bases ÷ 3 = 100.

items.q: A gene is 1500 bases long, of which 600 bases are in introns. How many amino acids does it code for? (Ignore start and stop codons.)
items.e: Only exons are translated: 900 bases ÷ 3 = 300.

items.e: Only exons are translated: 900 bases ÷ 3 = 300.

items.q: A gene is 900 bases long, of which 300 bases are in introns. How many amino acids does it code for? (Ignore start and stop codons.)
items.e: Only exons are translated: 600 bases ÷ 3 = 200.

items.q: What are introns?
c: non-coding sequences in genes that are removed from pre-mRNA
items.e: Exons are joined by splicing.

items.q: A DNA strand reads CGA CGG GTG. What is the complementary DNA strand?
items.e: In DNA, A pairs with T and G pairs with C.

items.q: A polypeptide has 127 amino acids. How many nucleotides (excluding the stop codon) are needed in its mRNA?
items.e: Each amino acid needs one codon of three bases: 3 × 127 = 381.

items.q: What is splicing?
c: removing introns and joining exons in the primary RNA transcript of eukaryotes
items.e: A cap and a poly-A tail are also added.

items.q: A mRNA has a reading frame of 190 codons, the last being a stop codon. How many amino acids are in the polypeptide?
items.e: The stop codon codes for no amino acid: 189.

items.q: A DNA template strand has the sequence ATCATTGCA. What is the sequence of the mRNA made from it?
items.e: mRNA is complementary to the template, with U instead of T.

items.q: Which tRNA anticodon pairs with the mRNA codon AGC?
items.e: The anticodon is complementary to the codon: A–U and G–C.

items.q: How can two cells with the same DNA, such as a nerve cell and a muscle cell, be so different?
c: one cell has lost its DNA
different genes are switched on (expressed) in each cell
items.e: Gene regulation controls differentiation.

items.q: A mRNA has a reading frame of 146 codons, the last being a stop codon. How many amino acids are in the polypeptide?
items.e: The stop codon codes for no amino acid: 145.

items.e: The stop codon codes for no amino acid: 280.

items.e: The stop codon codes for no amino acid: 172.

items.e: The stop codon codes for no amino acid: 83.

items.q: A DNA template strand has the sequence CCAAGTCCGCGC. What is the sequence of the mRNA made from it?
items.e: mRNA is complementary to the template, with U instead of T.

items.q: What is the start codon in mRNA?
items.e: UAA, UAG and UGA are stop codons.

items.q: A polypeptide has 133 amino acids. How many nucleotides (excluding the stop codon) are needed in its mRNA?
items.e: Each amino acid needs one codon of three bases: 3 × 133 = 399.

items.q: A DNA template strand has the sequence CATTCTACTTTA. What is the sequence of the mRNA made from it?
items.e: mRNA is complementary to the template, with U instead of T.

items.e: The stop codon codes for no amino acid: 81.

items.e: The stop codon codes for no amino acid: 294.

items.q: A DNA template strand has the sequence CTACCCGGCTGT. What is the sequence of the mRNA made from it?
items.e: mRNA is complementary to the template, with U instead of T.

items.q: What is the role of tRNA?
c: it carries the genetic code out of the nucleus
it carries a specific amino acid and has an anticodon that pairs with the mRNA codon
items.e: The anticodon is complementary to the codon.

items.q: A gene is 1500 bases long, of which 300 bases are in introns. How many amino acids does it code for? (Ignore start and stop codons.)
items.e: Only exons are translated: 1200 bases ÷ 3 = 400.

items.q: A DNA template strand has the sequence AATTAGTTCCTC. What is the sequence of the mRNA made from it?
items.e: mRNA is complementary to the template, with U instead of T.

items.q: mRNA: AGCAUGAAU. Codons: AAU = Asn, AGC = Ser, AUG = Met, UUC = Phe, UGU = Cys. What is the amino acid sequence?
items.e: Read the mRNA in triplets from the start: AGC AUG AAU.

items.q: mRNA: AAAACUGAU. Codons: AAA = Lys, ACU = Thr, GAU = Asp, CUU = Leu, AAU = Asn. What is the amino acid sequence?
items.e: Read the mRNA in triplets from the start: AAA ACU GAU.

items.q: mRNA: UCUACUAUU. Codons: ACU = Thr, AUU = Ile, UCU = Ser, AGC = Ser. What is the amino acid sequence?
items.e: Read the mRNA in triplets from the start: UCU ACU AUU.

items.q: mRNA: UAUGGCGCA. Codons: GCA = Ala, GGC = Gly, UAU = Tyr, UGG = Trp, AGC = Ser. What is the amino acid sequence?
items.e: Read the mRNA in triplets from the start: UAU GGC GCA.

items.q: Which tRNA anticodon pairs with the mRNA codon GAA?
items.e: The anticodon is complementary to the codon: A–U and G–C.

items.q: mRNA: UUCAGCGAU. Codons: AGC = Ser, GAU = Asp, UUC = Phe, GGC = Gly. What is the amino acid sequence?
items.e: Read the mRNA in triplets from the start: UUC AGC GAU.

items.q: Which tRNA anticodon pairs with the mRNA codon GCA?
items.e: The anticodon is complementary to the codon: A–U and G–C.

items.q: A DNA template strand has the sequence GTCCAGGTCGTG. What is the sequence of the mRNA made from it?
items.e: mRNA is complementary to the template, with U instead of T.

items.q: What is a homologous pair of chromosomes?
c: a pair of sex chromosomes only
two chromosomes with the same genes at the same loci
items.e: One comes from each parent.

items.q: A DNA template strand has the sequence AACTCGACT. What is the sequence of the mRNA made from it?
items.e: mRNA is complementary to the template, with U instead of T.

items.q: A DNA template strand has the sequence GCATGTTAAAGC. What is the sequence of the mRNA made from it?
items.e: mRNA is complementary to the template, with U instead of T.

items.q: What happens during translation?
c: tRNA anticodons pair with mRNA codons and amino acids are joined by peptide bonds
items.e: ATP is used to attach amino acids to tRNA.

items.q: mRNA: UCUCCUUGG. Codons: CCU = Pro, UCU = Ser, UGG = Trp, GAU = Asp, GUU = Val. What is the amino acid sequence?
items.e: Read the mRNA in triplets from the start: UCU CCU UGG.

items.q: A DNA template strand has the sequence ACTAGTTACCAT. What is the sequence of the mRNA made from it?
items.e: mRNA is complementary to the template, with U instead of T.

items.q: Where does transcription take place in eukaryotes?
items.e: RNA polymerase makes pre-mRNA.

items.q: mRNA: GUUUGGUGG. Codons: GUU = Val, UGG = Trp, CGU = Arg, CAA = Gln. What is the amino acid sequence?
items.e: Read the mRNA in triplets from the start: GUU UGG UGG.

items.q: A DNA template strand has the sequence CCGGTACGGGTT. What is the sequence of the mRNA made from it?
items.e: mRNA is complementary to the template, with U instead of T.

items.q: A DNA template strand has the sequence CAACTTGAGAGA. What is the sequence of the mRNA made from it?
items.e: mRNA is complementary to the template, with U instead of T.

items.q: mRNA: AAUAAUGCA. Codons: AAU = Asn, GCA = Ala, CAU = His, CAA = Gln. What is the amino acid sequence?
items.e: Read the mRNA in triplets from the start: AAU AAU GCA.

items.q: A DNA template strand has the sequence CACCAGTATCCT. What is the sequence of the mRNA made from it?
items.e: mRNA is complementary to the template, with U instead of T.

items.q: mRNA: UCUCCUUUU. Codons: CCU = Pro, UCU = Ser, UUU = Phe, CGU = Arg, AAU = Asn. What is the amino acid sequence?
items.e: Read the mRNA in triplets from the start: UCU CCU UUU.

items.q: How does decreased acetylation of histones affect a gene?
c: the chromatin becomes more condensed, so transcription is inhibited
items.e: Acetylation loosens chromatin.

items.q: How might high oestrogen levels increase the risk of breast cancer?
c: oestrogen can switch on genes that promote cell division
items.e: Fat tissue after the menopause makes oestrogen.

items.q: How can a substitution mutation stop a protein working?
c: it always makes the protein longer
it may change an amino acid in the active site so the shape changes
items.e: Or it may create a stop codon.

items.q: Why can different cells in one body make different proteins?
c: different genes are switched on (expressed) in each cell type
items.e: All body cells have the same genome.

items.q: What is RNA interference (RNAi)?
c: small RNA molecules bind to mRNA and stop it being translated
items.e: siRNA and miRNA are involved.

items.q: mRNA: AAUUGUACU. Codons: AAU = Asn, ACU = Thr, UGU = Cys, GAU = Asp, UCU = Ser. What is the amino acid sequence?
items.e: Read the mRNA in triplets from the start: AAU UGU ACU.

items.q: How does oestrogen switch on a gene?
c: it diffuses into the cell and binds to a receptor, releasing a transcription factor
items.e: The factor can then bind to DNA.

items.q: What is an oncogene?
c: a gene that stops cell division
a mutated proto-oncogene that is permanently switched on
items.e: It causes cells to divide too fast.

items.q: Why is it harder to find the proteome from the genome in complex organisms?
c: non-coding DNA and regulatory genes make it hard to predict the proteins
items.e: Alternative splicing also adds proteins.

items.q: A DNA template strand has the sequence GGTCCGTAC. What is the sequence of the mRNA made from it?
items.e: mRNA is complementary to the template, with U instead of T.

items.q: mRNA: AAAUUUAUU. Codons: AAA = Lys, AUU = Ile, UUU = Phe, GCU = Ala, CGU = Arg. What is the amino acid sequence?
items.e: Read the mRNA in triplets from the start: AAA UUU AUU.

items.q: What are induced pluripotent stem cells (iPS cells)?
c: adult cells reprogrammed to become pluripotent by switching on certain genes
items.e: Transcription factors are used.

items.q: What is the difference between benign and malignant tumours?
c: malignant tumours invade tissues and spread (metastasis)
benign tumours spread around the body
items.e: Benign tumours are usually enclosed.

items.q: What is an ethical issue with embryonic stem cells?
c: embryos are destroyed to obtain them
items.e: iPS cells avoid this.

items.q: Why is the genetic code described as non-overlapping?
c: each base is read in only one triplet
only half the bases are read
items.e: Triplets are read one after another.

items.q: Why is the genetic code described as universal?
c: all organisms have the same genes
the same triplets code for the same amino acids in almost all organisms
items.e: This is evidence of a common origin.

items.q: What is a unipotent stem cell?
c: one that can only become one type of cell
one that can become any cell
items.e: For example cardiomyocytes from heart stem cells.

items.q: Why might a base substitution have no effect on the protein?
c: the new triplet may code for the same amino acid
items.e: Because the code is degenerate.

items.q: mRNA: GCACAUAAU. Codons: AAU = Asn, CAU = His, GCA = Ala, GGU = Gly, UGU = Cys. What is the amino acid sequence?
items.e: Read the mRNA in triplets from the start: GCA CAU AAU.
